collections.title: Video & Brand Content
collections.description: Motion graphics, advertising and brand films.

projects.title: Colour in Motion
projects.subtitle: A sculptural world built around one bold colour.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.body: Imagine a short brand film for a design-led product launch. The idea is to communicate energy and confidence through colour, material and movement, without relying on a long explanation or a product feature list.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body: The visual direction pairs translucent orange glass with a matte cobalt sphere and a brushed-metal accent. Each material has a different relationship with light. The contrast creates a clear focal point while leaving room for movement, close-ups and graphic compositions.

sections.heading: The approach
sections.body:
### Find the visual language
Explore colour, silhouette and material combinations before settling on a small, coherent family of objects.

### Build the movement
Block out the camera and object choreography so that every shot has a clear beginning, focal point and transition.

### Shape the final film
Refine lighting and pacing, then prepare consistent compositions for the main film and shorter social cuts.

sections.heading: Deliverables
sections.body:
- Main brand-film concept
- Short-form campaign cutdowns
- Still-image art direction
- Wide and vertical composition studies

projects.title: The Launch
projects.subtitle: A product reveal that earns its moment.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.body: Develop a launch-film concept that introduces a new object gradually, using light and close-up detail to create anticipation before the complete reveal.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body: Start with abstract details of the surface, then let wider compositions reveal how the parts relate. A restrained palette keeps the focus on the object, while the progression from detail to silhouette gives the film a simple narrative.

sections.heading: The approach
sections.body:
### Define the reveal
Choose the one product quality the viewer should remember and build a shot sequence around it.

### Explore the surfaces
Study reflections, edges and material contrast to make close-up shots visually distinct.

### Design the campaign set
Adapt the main compositions into teaser frames, launch visuals and short social edits.

sections.heading: Deliverables
sections.body:
- Reveal-film treatment
- Teaser concepts
- Campaign key visuals
- Social-format adaptations

projects.title: Play it Again
projects.subtitle: A compact idea with room to repeat.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.body: Create a family of short social visuals that feels consistent across a campaign while giving each post a recognisable moment of its own.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body: Treat colour, objects and camera angles as a small visual toolkit. Repeat the underlying rhythm, then vary scale, composition and the way the objects meet. The system is intended to be flexible enough for new messages without losing its character.

sections.heading: The approach
sections.body:
### Set the rules
Define the palette, object family and pacing that make the series recognisable.

### Explore variations
Test a few distinct movements and crops against the same visual rules.

### Prepare the formats
Plan loops and end frames for square, portrait and vertical placements.

sections.heading: Deliverables
sections.body:
- Motion-system concept
- Looping social studies
- Format guidelines
- Campaign stills

collections.title: 3D & Animation
collections.description: Character design, animation and look development.

projects.title: Meet Momo
projects.subtitle: A little orange character. A lot of personality.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.body: Explore a character that could make an animation-led creative portfolio feel welcoming and recognisable. The character should read clearly at a small size, feel expressive in a still frame and suggest movement without needing an explanation.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body: Momo combines a soft, rounded silhouette with bright orange fur and oversized cobalt headphones. The open pose, eye direction and simple colour contrast establish a cheerful personality. A clean lavender environment leaves the silhouette and expression in focus.

sections.heading: The approach
sections.body:
### Find the personality
Define the mood and the key character traits before exploring proportions, pose and expression.

### Develop the look
Balance the tactile fur with clean accessories and soft studio lighting.

### Plan the performance
Identify a small set of expressive poses and movement ideas that could form the basis of an animation test.

sections.heading: Deliverables
sections.body:
- Character visual direction
- Colour and material study
- Hero composition
- Proposed pose and animation direction

projects.title: Soft Spot
projects.subtitle: An exploration of warmth, texture and expression.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.body: Study how surface texture and soft lighting can give a simple character a distinct emotional quality, while keeping the face and silhouette readable.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body: Use the orange fur as the main material and the headphones as a contrasting hard surface. Broad, soft lighting reveals volume without flattening the texture. The background remains quiet so that expression, shape and colour carry the composition.

sections.heading: The approach
sections.body:
### Choose the contrast
Pair one tactile material with one clean surface to create a useful visual tension.

### Study the lighting
Explore light direction and softness to preserve both texture and facial readability.

### Refine the composition
Check the balance between the character, negative space and background colour.

sections.heading: Deliverables
sections.body:
- Material mood study
- Lighting direction
- Character presentation concept
- Composition references

projects.title: Good Vibrations
projects.subtitle: A character performance inspired by rhythm.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.body: Develop a short performance idea in which a character’s reaction to music becomes the story. The intended feeling is spontaneous and playful, with a clear sequence that can also work as a loop.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body: Build the performance around anticipation, a moment of release and a soft recovery. Keep the silhouette easy to read and let the head, body and accessories react at slightly different times to suggest weight and personality.

sections.heading: The approach
sections.body:
### Map the beat
Decide where the main gesture happens and how the performance prepares for it.

### Explore the poses
Plan a small number of strong poses before refining the transitions between them.

### Close the loop
Design the recovery so that the last pose can lead naturally into the first.

sections.heading: Deliverables
sections.body:
- Performance treatment
- Pose-sequence proposal
- Timing direction
- Loop concept

collections.title: Interactive & Games
collections.description: Game art, environments and interaction design.

projects.title: A Little Leap
projects.subtitle: A small adventure between floating worlds.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.body: Imagine a light-hearted platforming world built around a simple action: one small rabbit making the next jump. The environment should make the route readable while still rewarding the player’s curiosity.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body: Floating islands create a clear relationship between the current platform and the next destination. Soft blue atmosphere separates the background from the foreground, while the orange rabbit remains easy to follow. Rounded forms and warm terrain support an inviting tone.

sections.heading: The approach
sections.body:
### Define the experience
Start with the intended feeling and the core action before adding environmental detail.

### Build a readable world
Arrange platforms, silhouettes and colour contrast so that the next destination feels clear.

### Plan a playable slice
Outline a small sequence of jumps to test scale, pacing and the relationship between art and interaction.

sections.heading: Deliverables
sections.body:
- Environment visual concept
- Character and world palette
- Platform-layout direction
- Prototype scope proposal

projects.title: Daydream
projects.subtitle: A world that feels soft, spacious and a little impossible.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.body: Explore an environment with a clear sense of depth and a memorable atmosphere. The scene should feel generous and inviting while keeping the foreground action visually distinct.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body: Layers of floating terrain, soft clouds and distant structures establish depth. A limited pastel palette ties the scene together, with warmer tones reserved for surfaces close to the character. Architectural fragments suggest a wider world without explaining all of it.

sections.heading: The approach
sections.body:
### Set the atmosphere
Choose a palette and lighting direction that support the mood of the world.

### Organise the layers
Separate foreground, midground and background through scale, contrast and colour.

### Guide the eye
Place landmarks and areas of negative space to create clear visual routes through the scene.

sections.heading: Deliverables
sections.body:
- Environment mood concept
- Palette and atmosphere direction
- Landmark exploration
- Scene-composition study

projects.title: Hopscotch
projects.subtitle: One simple mechanic. Plenty of room to play.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.body: Outline a compact game idea based on approachable jumping mechanics. The aim is to create a clear first interaction and introduce variety gradually, without overwhelming the player.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body: Use a short sequence of platforms to establish timing, distance and recovery. Each new layout can introduce one change, such as a wider gap or a smaller landing area. The visual direction keeps the intended destination clear and the tone light.

sections.heading: The approach
sections.body:
### Start with one action
Define the controls and the feedback for a single satisfying jump.

### Introduce variation
Plan small changes in spacing and rhythm, with each section teaching one new idea.

### Test the experience
Use a prototype to evaluate readability and pacing before committing to full production art.

sections.heading: Deliverables
sections.body:
- Core-mechanic outline
- Interaction-flow proposal
- Level-pacing sketch
- Prototype test plan
